transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic? What's been going on that made you decide to seek help?

Well, my regular doctor is the one who sent me here. My weight has dropped pretty low recently, and everyone is making a huge fuss over it. But honestly, I don't really see the problem. I'm a carpenter, and I feel like being this light helps me keep up with things in the shop. It keeps me from getting slowed down. So, I'm mostly just here because they insisted on it.
Have you been deliberately eating less food or controlling what you eat to maintain or achieve your current weight?

Well, yes, I suppose I do. 

On workshop days, I usually just have tea... maybe a few careful bites of something small, but that's about it. Stopping for a real meal just feels unnecessary to me. Honestly, it just throws off the control I've got over the day. I prefer to keep things strict so I can just focus and keep moving.
Do you ever have episodes where you eat a large amount of food in a short period of time, where you feel like you've lost control during that eating?

No, I don't have episodes like that. I don't eat large amounts of food at all, really. Like I mentioned, I prefer to keep a tight grip on what I eat, so... no, losing control and eating a lot just isn't something I do.
Besides controlling what you eat, do you do anything else to prevent weight gain or to 'undo' eating — such as making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or exercising excessively?

No, I don't do any of that. I don't make myself sick or take anything like laxatives. And as for exercise, well, my job is physical enough. I'm on my feet all day at the shop, lifting wood, moving around... so I don't feel the need to go out of my way to do extra workouts or anything. I just stick to keeping my eating strict.

When you look at yourself in the mirror or think about your body, do you feel like you're overweight or that parts of your body are too fat, even though others have expressed concern about your weight being too low?

I don't really see what other people see, I guess. People tell me I'm too thin, but when I look in the mirror, I just see areas that still need work. I wouldn't say I feel completely overweight, but there's definitely fat on my stomach and thighs that I need to get rid of. It just feels like I'm not done yet, no matter what anyone else says.
How long has this pattern of restricting your eating and the weight loss been going on? When did it start?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. It's hard to put an exact date on when it started. It just sort of... became the way I do things over time. I haven't really been keeping track of how long it's been going on, it's just my normal routine now.
Even though you can't pinpoint an exact date, do you think this pattern of strict eating and weight loss has been going on for at least a few months now, or has it been longer than that?

I suppose... yeah, it's definitely been at least a few months. Probably longer, if I really think about it. It just kind of crept up on me, so it's hard to say exactly, but yes, it's been going on for a while now.
When you think back, can you remember roughly when this strict eating pattern started? Was it within the last year, or has it been going on for longer than a year?

I really couldn't give you an exact timeframe. I mean, I don't know if it was within the last year or if it's been longer than that. Like I said, it just kind of became my normal way of doing things, so I haven't been keeping track of the months or years. It's just... how I live now.

When you say there's fat on your stomach and thighs that needs to go, how important is that concern to you in deciding to eat so little? Is avoiding weight gain or losing more weight one of your main goals right now?

Yes, it's very important. Honestly, avoiding weight gain is exactly why I eat the way I do. If I eat anything heavy, or... well, if I let myself have the kinds of foods we used to make for the holidays, I start worrying right away. I just get so anxious that I'll gain weight and lose the grip I've worked so hard to keep. So, yes, making sure I don't put any weight back on is definitely my main focus right now.
